objective: Proof and computation. A linear system over a finite chain ring (Z_(p^k), fields, Galois rings) that fails globally leaves, after any equation is removed, solutions whose top layer (residues mod the maximal ideal) has exactly the dimension a field would give: one line for the square systems of a substrate. So a knot kept inside a globally failing space has at most one variable taking all values and hides at most k - 1 digits; over a field nothing survives (ticket A's rigidity). Checked over Z_(p^k) and by brute force over F2[t]/(t^2); the bound is attained.
status: Proved by RIGID-SELECTION-20261101-001D-P001: a linear system over a finite chain ring that fails globally has m <= n + 1, and after removing any equation its solutions form a coset of R^(n-m+1) + N with N killed by pi^(k-1), so their top layer has exactly the dimension a field would give (one line for a substrate); hence fields are rigid, and a knot kept over Z_(p^k) has at most one full-range variable and hides at most k - 1 digits (attained over Z4, Z8, Z16, Z9, Z27, Z25); checked over nine rings Z_(p^k) and by brute force over F2[t]/(t^2)
title: Selection spends the top layer
